headline: Approved several revised school policies, personnel recommendations, MOUs with Harbor Homes and NASAS, and a $5,000 donation to Ledge Street School.
summary: The board approved updates to multiple policies covering surveillance, grant funds, discrimination, homeless student admission, and data retention. It approved personnel recommendations, a memorandum of understanding with Harbor Homes for student therapy services, a memorandum of understanding with NASAS changing special education coordinators' work year, and a $5,000 donation to the Ledge Street School Food Service Program.
decisions: Approved Policy ECAF on surveillance and audio or video recording by the district, 9-0.
Rescinded Policy EEAA on video and audio surveillance on school property, 9-0.
Approved Policy BGAA on policy development, adoption and review, 9-0.
Approved Policy JFABD on admission of homeless children and unaccompanied youth, 9-0.
Approved Policy AC-R1 on transgender and non-conforming staff (renamed), 9-0.
Approved Policy ACA on discrimination and harassment policy and grievance procedure, 9-0.
Approved Policy AC-R2, the sexual discrimination appendix (renamed), 9-0.
Approved Policy EHB on data records retention, 9-0.
Approved Policy DAF on administration of federal grant funds, 9-0.
Approved the Memorandum of Understanding between Harbor Homes, Inc., and the Nashua School District for the 2026-27 school year, 9-0.
Approved the Memorandum of Understanding between NASAS and the BOE updating the Special Educator Coordinator(s) work year, 9-0.
Accepted the $5000 donation to the Ledge Street School Food Service Program dated September 3, 2026, 8-0.

1 
  
BOARD OF EDUCATION 
MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 14, 2026 
NHS NORTH BOARD ROOM 
 
A meeting of the Board of Education was held at NHS North on Monday, September 14, 2026.  Ms. Bishop 
called the meeting to order at 6:06 pm and asked Ms. Raymond to read the opening statement and Mr. 
Johnson to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
Present: Ms. Giglio, Ms. Prinn, Mr. Johnson, Ms. Raymond, Ms. Lewis, Mr. Salvi, Ms. Lamphier,  
Ms. Lopez, Ms. Bishop 
 
Also Present:  Dr. Andrade, Dr. Scarpati, Mr. O’Rourke 
Also Present:  Members of the Public, Channel 99 Videographer 
 Student Representatives Saanvi Praturu (South) 
 
CONSENT AGENDA 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve the Consent Agenda.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
ITEMS REMOVED FROM CONSENT AGENDA 
 
COMMUNICATIONS OUTSIDE THE CONSENT AGENDA 
 
PUBLIC QUESTION/COMMENT PERIOD LIMITED TO ITEMS ON THIS AGENDA 
Stephen Scaer, Nashua 
• Mr. Scaer speaks against Policy AC-R1. 
Beth Scaer, Nashua 
• Ms. Scaer speaks against Policy AC-R1. 
 
SUPERINTENDENT’S COMMENTS 
• Dr. Andrade described a smooth school opening and thanked administrators, central-office staff, plant 
operations, and professional-development leaders. 
• Professional development focused on elementary literacy and writing, secondary curriculum 
mapping, and independent writing. 
• Fall athletics included more than 1,100 students across middle and high schools. 
• A community survey, special education and English-language-learning listening sessions were 
announced. 
 
 
BOARD RESPONSE TO SUPERINTENDENT’S COMMENTS 
• Members praised the opening of school and professional development. 
• The board discussed tracking athletic participation by students with IEPs and English-language 
supports. 
• Staffing and the challenge of implementing the strategic plan consistently across 18 schools was 
highlighted. 
 
STUDENT REPRESENTATIVE COMMENTS 
• It has been a smooth start so far. 
• Good to be back, although summer was too short. 
• Battle of the Bridge starts next week…GO SOUTH. 
 
COMMITTEE ON BUDGET
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  September 14, 2026 
 
 
2 
 
COMMITTEE ON FINANCE AND OPERATIONS 
 
COMMITTEE ON POLICY 
• Ms. Raymond informed board of the many changes to policies associated with legal updates and new 
laws that took effect for the beginning of the school year. 
• Policy ECAF (amended) combines our previous policy EEAA, which is video and audio surveillance 
on school property, with the old ECAF cameras on school busses, and it updates it to comply with the 
parental bill of rights and a new bill that was passed this year that authorizes districts to have 
outward-facing cameras on school busses for catching traffic violations.   
• This policy also outlines how any video or audio recordings are stored and who specifically is 
allowed to have access to them.   
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve Policy ECAF - Surveillance and Other Audio 
or Video Recording by the District.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to rescind Policy EEAA - Video and Audio Surveillance 
on School Property.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve Policy BGAA - Policy Development, Adoption 
and Review.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve Policy JFABD - Admission of Homeless 
Children and Unaccompanied Youth.  
 
• Board members questioned the term “homeless” versus “unhoused”.  The board reflected on this last 
year but kept the legal term to avoid any legal ambiguity. 
 
 Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve Policy AC-R1 - Transgender and Non-
Conforming Staff (renamed).  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve Policy ACA - Discrimination and Harassment:  
Policy and Grievance Procedure.   
 
• The District Title IX coordinator reviewed and red-lined changes to the school board association’s 
model policy to reflect Nashua practices.  This policy details the reporting process if someone feels 
like they have been discriminated against, from staff to students.  
 
Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve Policy AC-R2 - Sexual Discrimination 
Appendix (renamed).  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve Policy EHB - Data Records Retention.  Motion 
passes 9-0.
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  September 14, 2026 
 
 
3 
• Policy DAF was amended to fully comply with both federal and state law regarding grant funding.  
Sections 11, 12, and 13 were added.  The threshold for purchases was changed from $250,000 to 
$350,000, and again on page 11 regarding competitive bids.  In addition, micro-purchases was 
changed from $10,000 to $15,000. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve Policy DAF - Administration of Federal Grant 
Funds.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Motion passes 9-0. 
 
• The next policy meeting will address policies on FMLA, religious neutrality, and bullying. 
 
 
COMMITTEE ON HUMAN RESOURCES  
 
Ms. Bishop moved, seconded by Ms. Giglio, to suspend the rules to consider items from the HR meeting 
held earlier this evening.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Lopez, to approve the September 14, 2026 Personnel 
Recommendations.  Motion passes 9-0.

NEW BUSINESS 
• The District provides space in our buildings to Harbor Homes for student therapy services; the district 
does not oversee treatment or effectiveness. 
• Harbor Homes provided a presentation of data from previous years’ service. 
 
Ms. Bishop moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the Memorandum of Understanding between 
Harbor Homes, Inc., and the Nashua School District for 2026-27 school year.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
• The MOU with NASAS is to address the changing the work year for three special education 
coordinator positions from 260 to 214 days. 
 
Ms. Bishop moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to approve the Memorandum of Understanding between the 
NASAS and the BOE to update language in the current contract regarding the Special Educator 
Coordinator(s) work year.  Motion passes 9-0.
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  September 14, 2026 
 
 
4 
• Dr. Andrade presented the $5000 donation to Ledge Street School to help fund students with past due 
balances.   
• All board members graciously thanked the donor for their generosity and commitment to the 
community. 
 
Mr. Salvi stepped out. 
 
Ms. Lopez moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to accept the $5000 donation to the Ledge Street School Food 
Service Program dated September 3, 2026.  Motion passes 8-0. 
 
 
UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
 
 
LIAISON REPORTS 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT 
• None 
 
 
BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS 
• JSSBC approved obtaining a roof-replacement quote for Bicentennial. 
• The board thanked all employees for stepping up. 
• Board members thanked district employees and the donor supporting student meals. 
 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Lopez, to adjourn.  So voted at 7:10 pm. 
 
 
Submitted by Tara C. Kinsella
